name: MI-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat after Thanedar lost renomination, but Democratic nominee McKinney heavily funded
Prediction markets price Democratic win near certain
Republican nominee has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: The seat sits in a D+22 district and the Democratic nominee has raised over $1.3 million with outside backing, while the Republican nominee reports no fundraising and markets price a Democratic win at 98%. The open-seat status barely moves a district this blue.
model.watch: A surprise third-party or independent surge, or a major scandal involving the Democratic nominee, would be needed to put this in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Shri Thanedar (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Detroit-area MI-13 is one of the most Democratic districts in the country, with a partisan lean of D+22. Incumbent Shri Thanedar lost renomination, so the seat is open, but the Democratic nominee Donavan McKinney enters the general with strong resources: about $1.4 million raised and roughly $930,000 in outside support. The Republican nominee has no reported fundraising or outside spending, and minor-party and independent candidates lack visible resources.

Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability at 98 percent. With no general-election polls available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic hold in the mid-20s margin range.
